result.topic_en: The page derives the Euler–Lagrange equation N − dP/dx + ddQ/dx² − … = 0 as the condition for the integral ∫Z dx to be a maximum or minimum, by requiring the integral part of the variation to vanish for an arbitrary local variation δy. It then remarks that this is the same equation as in Euler's earlier Treatise, now obtained from purely analytic principles.
result.transcription:
108 DE METHODO
in quibus formulis, quatenus differentialia superiorum graduum inuoluunt, differentiale $dx$ constans est assumtum. At $\delta y$ pro singulis valoribus ipsius $x$ valorem habet arbitrarium.

XXIII.
Si igitur pro valore $x=a$ formula $\int Z dx$ maxima vel minima fieri debeat, incrementum modo inuentum, si in eo statuatur $x=a$, nihilo aequale poni oportet; hocque ita vt semper euanescat, quomodocunque variationes $\delta y$ assumantur. Quare etiam, si talis variatio vnico cuipiam valori $y$, qui conuenit valori cuicunque ipsius $x$, minori quam $a$, tribuatur, expressio inuenta in nihilum abire debet. Tum autem nulla mutatio inde valoribus vltimis ipsius $y$, qui ipsi $x=a$ respondent, inducuntur; quare cum, posito $x=a$, pars incrementi absoluta $\delta y(P-\frac{dQ}{dx}+\frac{ddR}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3S}{dx^3}+\text{etc.})$
$+\frac{d\delta y}{dx}(Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+\frac{ddS}{dx^2}-\text{etc.})+\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}(R-\frac{dS}{dx}+\text{etc.})$
$+\text{etc.}$ tantum ab vltimorum ipsius $y$ valorum variatione pendeat, pro iis erit $\delta y=0$, $d\delta y=0$, $dd\delta y=0$ etc. sicque haec pars sponte euanescit. Ex quo necesse est, vt sola pars integralis seorsim nihilo aequalis reddatur, indeque fieri debeat:
$\int dx\,\delta y\left(N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-\text{etc.}\right)=0.$

XXIV.
Haec autem expressio summam omnium variationum, quae ex singulorum ipsius $y$ variationibus nascuntur, complectitur; sed quia talis mutatio in vnico valore fieri concipitur, tota summa ad hanc vnam variationem

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 109
riationem reducitur, reliquis omnibus euanescentibus; quare necesse est, vt pro hoc casu sit
$N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-\text{etc.}=0.$
Quoniam vero, in quocunque loco haec variatio fieri concipiatur, natura maximi minimi ve aeque hanc annihilationem postulat, necesse est, vt pro omnibus valoribus ipsius $x$ sit $N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-\text{etc.}=0$; quae ergo aequatio continet relationem indefinitam inter $x$ et $y$, qua efficitur, vt inde oriundus valor formulae integralis $\int Z dx$ fiat maximus vel minimus, posito $x=a$, vnde patet, hanc relationem non ab ista quantitate $a$ pendere.

XXV.
Haec iam est eadem aequatio, quam pro solutione eiusdem problematis olim in Tractatu meo de Maximis ac Minimis dedi; nunc autem ex meris principiis analyticis deriuaui; quod negotium ideo commode successit, quod singulis valoribus ipsius $y$ variationes accedere assumsi, quibus in statum variatum transferantur. Deinde vero reductio formularum integralium §. 21. facta negotium penitus confecit, qua illae ita fuerunt in partes resolutae, vt aliae a signo summatorio $\int$ essent liberae, quae autem eo manserunt adstrictae, eae tantum ipsam variationem $\omega=\delta y$, sine eius differentialibus, inuoluerent; quo ipso hoc commodi sumus nacti, vt, cum quaelibet variatio seorsim ad nihilum perduci debeat, formula integralis statim praebuerit aequationem
$N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\text{etc.}=0,$

items.quote: Si igitur pro valore $x=a$ formula $\int Z dx$ maxima vel minima fieri debeat, incrementum modo inuentum, si in eo statuatur $x=a$, nihilo aequale poni oportet
items.english: If therefore the formula ∫Z dx is to become a maximum or minimum for the value x=a, the increment just found must be set equal to zero when x=a is put in it.

items.quote: necesse est, vt pro omnibus valoribus ipsius $x$ sit $N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-\text{etc.}=0$
items.english: It is necessary that for all values of x we have N − dP/dx + ddQ/dx² − d³R/dx³ + d⁴S/dx⁴ − etc. = 0.

items.quote: vnde patet, hanc relationem non ab ista quantitate $a$ pendere
items.english: Whence it is clear that this relation does not depend on the quantity a.

items.quote: Haec iam est eadem aequatio, quam pro solutione eiusdem problematis olim in Tractatu meo de Maximis ac Minimis dedi; nunc autem ex meris principiis analyticis deriuaui
items.english: This is now the same equation that I formerly gave for the solution of the same problem in my Treatise on Maxima and Minima; but now I have derived it from purely analytic principles.
